pr_title: roachprod: use NVMe when provisioning clusters on Azure.
pr_body:
Currently, when provisioning clusters on Azure, we interface with the
 data disk via SCSI (the default). For improved performance and
 uniformity with other clouds use NVMe.

 Azure support DiskControllerType NVMe for `E Series v5` VM family.
 OS disk and network disks are interfaced with NVMe.
 Local storage are interfaced via SCSI, NVMe is not supported for
 local disk.

 Changes as part of this PR:
  - For `E Series v5` VM family enabled NVMe.

Epic: none
Fixes: #129009

Release note: None

issue_context.title: roachprod: use NVMe when provisioning clusters on Azure
issue_context.body:
Currently, when provisioning clusters on Azure, we interface with the data disk via SCSI (the default):

```
ubuntu@renato-test-0001:~$ lsblk | grep mnt
└─sdb1    8:17   0   100G  0 part /mnt
ubuntu@renato-test-0001:~$ lsscsi 
[0:0:0:0]    disk    Msft     Virtual Disk     1.0   /dev/sda 
[1:0:1:0]    disk    Msft     Virtual Disk     1.0   /dev/sdb 
[5:0:0:0]    cd/dvd  Msft     Virtual CD/ROM   1.0   /dev/sr0 
```

We should (for improved performance and uniformity with other clouds) use NVMe. The Azure API supports passing a `DiskControllerType` option to the `StorageProfile` [1], which we should set to NMVe. However, that option is only available starting on version `2022-08-01` and we are currently using `2021-07-01`.

Tasks:

- [ ] upgrade our SDK to at least  `2022-08-01`
- [ ] Set `DiskControllerType` to `NVMe` when creating VMs
- [ ] We should then also be able to revert #128843

[1] https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.azure.management.compute.models.storageprofile.diskcontrollertype?view=azure-dotnet-legacy#microsoft-azure-management-compute-models-storageprofile-diskcontrollertype

Jira issue: CRDB-41329

> Out of curiosity, was there a particular reason to not use b VMs in roachtest? 

I may have missed their availability. If I understand correctly (insofar as it's possible, given Azure's labyrinth of instance types), we could use `Ebsv5` [1], but it's the only family which supports Cascade Lake and NVMe with remote storage.

[1] https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/ebdsv5-ebsv5-series#ebsv5-series-nvme
Should i raise a follow up PR to include `Ebsv5` in machine type selection logic?

> Should i raise a follow up PR to include `Ebsv5` in machine type selection logic?

Sure, let's create a new tracking issue. Tbh, I'm not too enthusiastic about this instance type. It's nearly double the price of its GCE analog `n2-highmem`, which seems like a high price to pay just to get NVMe. Further, the limited availability means we could only rely on benchmarking "highmem" configurations.
Yeah, it seems like it's not worth it for now. I think a `TODO` to revisit this in the `machine_type.go` file is sufficient.
